You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

> about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- EDGAR's filing history for the merged entity's own CIK (0001647339) shows no periodic
  report (10-K, 10-Q, or otherwise) filed after its fiscal-year-2017 Form 10-K and its
  final closing-day filings; no Form 10-K or 10-Q for any later fiscal year appears in
  its filing history. [SRC: SEC EDGAR company filing history for CIK 0001647339]
- The surviving public reporting entity (CIK 0001467373) continued filing annual
  reports on Form 10-K without interruption after the transaction, including for the
  fiscal years ended August 31, 2018 through August 31, 2025; this entity's own
  consolidated financial statements already incorporated the results of the merged
  subsidiary before the transaction closed. [SRC: SEC EDGAR company filing history for CIK 0001467373]

## Absence of transaction-specific disclosure in the outcome window
- The surviving entity's Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended August 31, 2021 (filed
  October 15, 2021), which falls within the ~3-5-year window after the ~2017-2018
  transaction, contains no reference to "Accenture Holdings," the internal merger, or
  the eliminated holding-company tier anywhere in its text. [SRC: SEC accession 0001467373-21-000229, Form 10-K for fiscal year ended August 31, 2021]
- No segment, business-unit, or subsidiary-level disclosure in that Form 10-K
  distinguishes results attributable to the formerly separate legal entity from the
  surviving entity's ordinary consolidated operating results. [SRC: SEC accession 0001467373-21-000229, Form 10-K for fiscal year ended August 31, 2021]

## No distinguishable business-specific outcome record
- Because the merged entity was, at closing, a holding company whose own registration
  terminated the same day the transaction completed, and because its results were
  already consolidated into the surviving public entity's financial statements before
  closing, there is no post-closing public disclosure — by either the merged entity
  (which stopped reporting) or the surviving entity (whose later reports do not name or
  segment the transaction) — that separately documents a realized trajectory for "the
  acquired business" distinct from the surviving entity's own ordinary continuing
  operations. This case's outcome is not separately observable from public records and
  is coded uncertain / no distinguishable business-specific record for the ~3-5-year
  window. [SRC: SEC EDGAR company filing history for CIK 0001647339; SRC: SEC accession 0001467373-21-000229, Form 10-K for fiscal year ended August 31, 2021]

[SLICE END]
